goal: WAVE 5: finish every buildable gap with real backend integration on Nano + offline (config_only enforced, buildable not_simulated built, engine-coverage limits lifted)

depth_targets.title: Default encryption
limitations: Every PutObject/GetObject/HeadObject/CopyObject/CompleteMultipartUpload response carries x-amz-server-side-encryption (and the KMS key id / bucket-key header when configured) reflecting the bucket's default-encryption setting — AES256 by default, matching S3's own always-on default — but objects are not actually encrypted at rest.

depth_targets.title: Block public access (bucket settings)
limitations: PutBucketAcl/PutObjectAcl with a public canned ACL (public-read, public-read-write, authenticated-read) is rejected with AccessDenied when BlockPublicAcls is on, and PutBucketPolicy is rejected when the policy is public (Principal "*", Effect Allow) and BlockPublicPolicy is on. Existing grants/policies already stored before the block was enabled are not retroactively revoked, and Vyomi does not authenticate requests, so there is no per-request anonymous-access check.

depth_targets.title: Bucket policy
limitations: PutBucketPolicy validates the document is well-formed JSON and is rejected (see Block Public Access) when it is public and blocked; otherwise the policy is stored and returned verbatim and is not evaluated for request authorization — Vyomi has no IAM principal/condition evaluator.

depth_targets.title: Lifecycle rules
limitations: Expiration rules are enforced, evaluated lazily on list/get/head: Date-based rules fire deterministically once the date has passed; Days-based rules use the real elapsed wall-clock (not accelerated), as in real S3. In a versioned bucket, expiration inserts a delete marker rather than destroying history. NoncurrentVersionExpiration, storage-class Transition actions and AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload are stored and returned but not yet enforced.

depth_targets.title: Cross-origin resource sharing (CORS)
limitations: OPTIONS preflight and the Access-Control-* response headers are enforced on actual GET/HEAD/PUT/DELETE requests whose Origin and method match a configured rule; this is wire-level header emulation of CORS, not a real browser's same-origin/CORS enforcement engine.

depth_targets.title: Object Ownership
limitations: BucketOwnerEnforced is enforced: every PutBucketAcl/PutObjectAcl call on the bucket is rejected (InvalidBucketAclWithObjectOwnership), matching real S3's "ACLs disabled" behaviour. BucketOwnerPreferred/ObjectWriter are stored and returned but have no further effect, since Vyomi has no per-request uploader identity to attribute ownership to.

depth_targets.title: Access control list (ACL)
limitations: Bucket and object ACLs are stored and returned (Get/PutBucketAcl, Get/PutObjectAcl); a canned ACL (private, public-read, public-read-write, authenticated-read) now produces the real grant list GetAcl returns. Writes are rejected under Block Public Access / BucketOwnerEnforced (see those capabilities), but grants are not evaluated for request authorization — Vyomi does not authenticate requests.

depth_targets.title: Object Lock
limitations: Object Lock can only be enabled at bucket creation (as in real S3) — PutObjectLockConfiguration on a bucket created without it returns InvalidBucketState. Legal hold (Put/GetObjectLegalHold) and retention (Put/GetObjectRetention, GOVERNANCE/COMPLIANCE) are enforced: DeleteObject for a held/retained version id is rejected, GOVERNANCE can be overridden with x-amz-bypass-governance-retention, COMPLIANCE cannot. A bucket-level default-retention rule is not yet stored.

depth_targets.title: Static website hosting
limitations: Put/Get/DeleteBucketWebsite store and return the index/error-document configuration verbatim, but static website hosting serves GET/HEAD over a separate bucket-name.s3-website-<region>.amazonaws.com HTTP origin; Vyomi's native wire is a single S3 control+data endpoint and does not run a per-bucket website origin, so that serving path does not exist.

depth_targets.title: Server access logging
limitations: Put/GetBucketLogging store and return the target bucket/prefix verbatim, but server access logging periodically writes delivery-log objects (one per time window) into that target bucket from S3's internal request-logging pipeline; Vyomi has no request-log writer producing those objects.

depth_targets.title: Event notifications
limitations: Offline appliance: events are delivered to the configured SQS queues, SNS topics and Lambda functions in this simulator (ObjectCreated, ObjectRemoved, DeleteMarkerCreated, TestEvent).
Nano: the configuration is stored and returned, but events are not delivered yet.

depth_targets.title: Replication rules
limitations: PutBucketReplication requires source-bucket Versioning Enabled (as real S3 does). Enabled rules are enforced SYNCHRONOUSLY on PutObject/CopyObject/CompleteMultipartUpload — a matching key is copied into its destination bucket immediately (no async replication-time delay), and the source version's GetObject/HeadObject response carries x-amz-replication-status: COMPLETED. Only destination buckets that exist in this same Vyomi appliance are reachable — real cross-account/cross-region destinations outside it are not. NoncurrentVersionReplication, delete-marker replication, RTC/metrics and replica-modification-sync are not yet enforced.

depth_targets.title: Transfer acceleration
limitations: Transfer acceleration only changes the network path (ingest via a CloudFront edge location) to the same S3 API — there is no behavioural difference for a client to observe, so there is nothing for a single-endpoint simulator to enforce or differentiate.

depth_targets.title: Requester pays
limitations: Put/GetBucketRequestPayment store and return the Payer setting (BucketOwner/Requester), but Requester Pays changes who is billed for data transfer and requests; Vyomi has no request-identity or billing model, so there is no payer to attribute cost to and no billing behaviour changes.

depth_targets.title: Intelligent-Tiering Archive configurations
limitations: Put/Get/List/DeleteBucketIntelligentTieringConfiguration store and return each named configuration verbatim, but Intelligent-Tiering archive configurations move objects between access tiers automatically based on 30/90+ day access-pattern windows; Vyomi does not run a long-horizon storage-class scheduler, so no object ever actually transitions tier.

depth_targets.title: Inventory configurations
limitations: Put/Get/List/DeleteBucketInventoryConfiguration store and return each named configuration verbatim, but inventory configurations run on a daily/weekly schedule and write a CSV/ORC/Parquet manifest of bucket contents to a destination bucket; Vyomi has no scheduler producing those exports.

depth_targets.title: Metrics
limitations: Put/Get/List/DeleteBucketMetricsConfiguration store and return each named request-metrics filter verbatim, but request/storage filter metrics publish to CloudWatch on a recurring schedule; Vyomi does not run a CloudWatch metrics pipeline for S3, so no metric data points are ever produced.
